fixes.what: The 1915 shape adds 4 cells at Tsingtao (120.35-120.56 E, 36.13-36.25 N; the Kiautschou leased territory) beside the 3 Micronesian cells, and the ledger has no event for them. The 1915 note says 'Nothing in the shape corresponds to the surrender ... (the page does not say where)', which is untrue for both the shape and the page. The cells stay in every shape to 1929 (and 8 cells from 1938), so the 1924-1931 keyframes and the 1929 outline used as the correction for 1932-1945 keep Tsingtao as direct Japanese land after its return to China in 1922.
fixes.why: Gazetteer: minus(Empire of Japan 1915, Empire of Japan 1911) = 7 cells, 4 of them at Qingdao. A Qingdao probe gives 4 cells in the 1915, 1917, 1920, 1922, 1924, 1926-1929 and 1932 shapes. Empire of Japan page (the author's own source): 'Japanese and allied British Empire forces soon moved to occupy Tsingtao fortress, the German East Asia Squadron base, German-leased territories in China's Shandong Province as well as the Marianas, Caroline, and Marshall Islands in the Pacific'; 'The German colonial troops surrendered on November 7, 1914, and Japan gained the German holdings.'
fixes.fix: Add occupation_start german-empire 1914-11 at Tsingtao/Kiautschou ({'place':'Qingdao','km':30}, confidence 3, Empire page) and the end in 1922 with the return to republic-of-china (open the Kiautschou Bay Leased Territory or Shandong Problem page for the year and month). Mark keyframes 1924-1931 adjust with a correction minus Qingdao, and use minus Qingdao in the 1932-1945 corrections; the 1938 reoccupation is part of the China occupation events. Add Tsingtao to the zones of /wars/3 and correct the 1915 note.

fixes.what: The China occupations are drawn as whole provinces (all of Hebei in July 1937, all of Zhejiang in December 1937, all of Shanxi in March 1938, all of Henan in June 1938), although the pages date only the cities. Western Henan fell only in the 1944 Ichi-Go offensive, which /ledger/47 does not cover.
fixes.why: Second Sino-Japanese War page: 'On 6 June, they captured Kaifeng, the capital of Henan'; 'In 1944, Japan launched Operation Ichi-Go, the invasion of Henan and Changsha'.
fixes.fix: Intersect each province with the Cliopatria shape of the year after (for example intersect(admin1 Henan, Empire of Japan 1939)), and add the rest of Henan to the 1944 Ichi-Go event with the Ichi-Go page.

fixes.what: The Tianjin cells (1 in 1898, 8 from 1900, 7 in 1929; about 2,000 km2) are kept as Japanese territory, and through the 1929 outline they sit in every correction to 1945. The dossier's own notes say 'concessions are not territory under rule 4 and are not recorded'.
fixes.why: A probe over 116.5-118 E and 38.5-40 N gives 1 cell in 1898, 8 in 1900-1926 and 7 in 1929. The real Japanese concession at Tianjin covered about 1 km2.
fixes.fix: Mark the 1898-1931 keyframes adjust with a correction minus the Tianjin cells (polygon 116.5-118 E, 38.5-40 N), and do the same in the 1932-1945 corrections, or explain in the note why they stay.

fixes.what: The Boshin War opponent is republic-of-ezo from January 1868 for all of northern Honshu and Hokkaido, and the whole remainder is gained in May 1869. By the reviewer's reading (to be confirmed on the Boshin War page), the Republic of Ezo was proclaimed only in the winter of 1868-1869 and held Hokkaido alone; northern Honshu was the Northern Alliance's and fell in 1868.
fixes.why: The Empire page (as quoted) dates only the end at Hakodate, May 1869; the war page was not opened (page budget). Confidence 1 and 2.
fixes.fix: Open the Boshin War page. Split the contest and gain into northern Honshu (1868, against the Ouetsu Reppan Domei or the shogunate's loyalists) and Hokkaido (republic-of-ezo, from its proclamation to 1869-5).

verdicts.summary: Validates (0 errors, 11 counterpart warnings). 19 events checked on 6 pages: 17 confirmed (3 of them confidence-3 events whose region is wider than the page, lowered to 2), 2 mis-dated at confidence 1-2 (both fixed by the reviewer). No fabricated event was found. Failed for two unapplied blocking findings: the Tsingtao/Kiautschou cells in the 1915-1932 shapes have no event, and the 1915 note denies what the shape and the page show (and the 1929 outline carries the cells into every correction to 1945); and the Ryukyu Domain vassalage (1872-1879) has no mirror for ryukyu-kingdom's ledger. The merge of 'Empire of Japan' and 'Japan' into one dossier is argued from the page and accepted.
